page: Microsoft Azure E4ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing hyperthreading. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, establishing a generous 8.0 GB of memory per core. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions.

Hardware resource provisioning excludes local storage disks, requiring deployments to depend on remote storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage. The instance configuration contains zero discrete GPUs and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing primary utility toward pure compute and memory tasks in networked environments.

Benchmark measurements show mid-range performance for single-core tasks, with stress-ng single-core compute, static web serving, and compression throughput falling within the median band. However, multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth across uncached blocks register in the lower performance quartile. Database operational tests and Redis operations similarly demonstrate lower comparative throughput, reflecting limits imposed by the 4-vCPU capacity and memory throughput characteristics under sustained parallel workloads.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance delivers practical resource balance for workloads prioritizing memory footprints over raw parallel core scaling. It is best aligned with memory-bound workloads such as intermediate in-memory caching tiers, lightweight relational database hosting, backend enterprise application middleware, and static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores alongside 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache with vector and matrix acceleration instructions such as AVX-512 and AMX. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring remote storage solutions, and includes no GPUs. Benchmark metrics display standard single-threaded CPU and encryption performance, while multi-core workloads, raw memory bandwidth, and database transaction tests register lower comparative throughput. The hardware profile offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-centric configurations that do not demand extensive parallel compute. It is positioned for workloads such as in-memory caches, small enterprise databases, background data processing, and medium-scale web applications.
